title: Book One · Chapter 108: Blue Beside Green
story:
At two on Sunday, Mum clears her sewing from the table.

She keeps one small tin beside the window. The rest goes onto her shelf. Dad spreads the old paper flat. He puts the wooden boat in the middle.

Ronan brings the blue paint. Dad opens it and mixes it slowly. It is grey-blue, the colour they chose together.

“We are keeping the green,” Ronan says.

“We are.”

They put a paper strip over the green end. It will protect the green paint from the blue. Dad puts a little paint on the brush. He shows it to Ronan. The brush needs only that small amount. Ronan tries on a spare piece first.

His first stroke makes a thick shiny patch. The second spreads it further than he expects.

“Less,” Dad says.

Ronan wipes a little paint from the brush as shown. The next stroke is thinner. The paint is thin. He can still see the wood below it.

Now he paints the plain end of the boat. The blue line is not quite straight along one side. He wants to add more paint. He wants a perfectly straight line.

Dad touches the paper beside it.

“Let us stop before the edge gets too thick.”

Ronan looks at the uneven line. The bend in it is small. He can see his own brush marks on the boat. The pale wood at this end is turning blue.

They turn it carefully. Now he can reach the other side. He keeps his hands off the wet paint. Dad holds a dry part. Ronan does the brush work.

Mum comes to look but does not lean over the fresh colour.

“That is a handsome boat.”

“Not finished yet,” Ronan says.

“No. It looks handsome now too.”

The first coat dries on the protected shelf. Dad cleans the brush properly. He puts the paint in a safe place. The children cannot reach it there. Mum gave Ronan a cloth just for this job. He wipes the table with it. He keeps it away from the kitchen towels.

They spend the waiting time in the yard. Leo comes to the gate, and Ronan shows him the boat through the window. Leo wants to touch it. “You can touch it later,” Ronan says. “The paint is wet now.” Leo accepts that and asks for the cloth ball instead.

The boys play while Dad sits by the door. Mum finishes her small sewing job. No one needs to watch the boat every minute. It can dry while the family does other things.

The next day, Dad checks the surface. Some parts need more paint. They add a little to those parts. By the following evening, the blue end is dry. Dad checks it again before Ronan lifts the boat.

Both ends have colour now. The original green remains. The new blue is not quite even along one edge. Ronan turns the boat in his hands. He runs a finger along the smooth dry wood below.

“Shall we put it in water?” Dad asks.

“Not now.”

“Why?”

“I want to look at it first.”

He puts it on the low shelf beside the book with the red sail. The bell stands a little further along. His old house picture is safe nearby. His old things are still here beside the boat. He kept them through the move and school days. Now the boat has blue paint beside its green.

Before bed, he tells Mum, “The school boat project is finished. My home boat is finished too.”

“For now,” she says.

Ronan nods. The paint work is finished. He can still play with it on another day. Tonight it stays dry on the shelf. He looks once more at the green and blue.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- coat＝涂层
- protect＝保护
- thin＝薄的
- for now＝目前

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：stroke＝一次刷动；surface＝表面；grey-blue＝灰蓝色。

## 读句提示

**The paint is wet now.**

颜料／现在／还是湿的。把“not until it is dry”的省略解释成眼前事实。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan怎样亲手参与木船上色？
2. 为什么木船最后没有立刻再次下水？
